Diego / Monica —

Thanks for the intro. We're kicking off the project to move our search index and rerank stack to Redwood-hosted embeddings and the managed reranker. A few quick constraints from our side before the kickoff:

- We have ~1.2B documents (mostly small blobs, average doc length ~600 chars) — need a realistic backfill strategy (can't take full downtime).
- Vector store must strictly support encryption at rest + VPC peering for initial pilot.
- Procurement needs a high-level cost estimate and SOW to approve budget (target internal approval by 5/6).
- We need the rerank eval to include our 1500-sample gold set and a production-like request distribution.

Can you share a short checklist for the staging cutover and any assumptions you need from us ahead of the kickoff? Also, Monday-Thursday mornings PT work best for our team.

Thanks,

Jill —

Appreciate the constraints. I've attached an initial operations checklist (embeddings-cutover-checklist.xlsx) that lays out a staged backfill approach we use for large indexes (seed + parallel hydrated shards + sync window). High level summary below, and we can walk the team through during the kickoff: 

1) Staging hydration: create a small, production-like index (5-10% of doc volume) using a representative subset for smoke tests and rerank evals.
2) Parallel backfill: run a distributed backfill pipeline (chunked, idempotent) to populate the final vector store while the read layer remains on the old index; keep the write-forwarding window small.
3) KV cache priming & warmup: run prefix caching for hot queries identified from your logs.
4) Cutover window: schedule an hourly cutover with automatic rollback to the old index if error rate exceeds threshold.
5) Post-cutover validation: rerank eval sweep + latency/cost sanity checks.

A few immediate asks to help size the plan:
- Can you share your top-10k query sample or sample query distribution?
- Which vector store(s) are you evaluating (self-hosted FAISS, managed Pinecone, Weaviate, etc.)? If you already prefer one, call it out so we can align the connector and schema.
- Any restraints on maintenance windows / blackout periods?

I propose a 30-min kickoff to align scope and owners. I'm available Wed 4/21 10:00–11:30 PT or Thu 4/22 09:00–12:00 PT.

Best,

Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Two points from CS side regarding the rerank eval:

- We prefer to run the eval against your gold set plus a stratified sample of tail queries (we typically target an additional 5k tail samples to surface regressions). Please send the gold set as a CSV with columns (query_id, query_text, ground_truth_doc_id).
- Give us a target NDCG / MRR threshold or a rollback rule (for example: if NDCG@10 drops > 3% on the gold set we halt cutover). If you don't have a strict threshold, we can propose one based on the initial staging run.

Also note: if you plan to use a managed vector DB, we need the network jtradeoffs for VPC peering and whether they support private endpoints. I'll add that to the checklist on our side.

Subject: Vector store choices & instrumentation checklist

Hey all —

A few notes on vector DB considerations for the pilot (Pinecone-focused):

- Connector & schema: we suggest normalizing embeddings to 1536-d floats (if using an open model, we can align to your existing embedding dim). Pinecone supports float32; if you plan to use quantized storage later we'll prototype a quantization layer and run accuracy checks in staging.
- Sharding & backfill: for 1.2B documents, we recommend sharded backfills using partition keys (e.g., by hashed doc_id) with a concurrency cap to avoid IO spikes. Backfill should be resumable and idempotent.
- Instrumentation: collect per-request token counts, embed latency, vector insert latency, and a per-query rerank delta metric (score_new - score_old). Add a tracing ID to correlate with your logs.
- Smoke tests: 1) sanity sample of 1k queries against staging, 2) 30-minute steady-state load at 2x expected QPS to surface latency tail, 3) NDCG sweep against the gold set.

I'll attach a short compat matrix that maps features (encryption at rest, private endpoints, per-index TTLs) across the providers we commonly see.

-Karthik
